Tap to Wake listing copy vs display engineering — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate system wake gestures with storefront language. iOS Settings and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Tap to Wake on the device — when enabled, tapping the iPhone screen wakes the lock screen when the phone is already face-up and the display is off — so you can glance at notifications or the time without pressing Side or Home buttons. Toggle under Settings → Display & Brightness → Tap to Wake (轻点唤醒). System behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Raise to Wake on the device — lifting or picking up the iPhone from a flat surface wakes the display. Different gesture, different buyer vocabulary. Covered on our Raise to Wake listing guide — not this page unless your English listing conflates both; we keep scope accurate.
  • Tap-to-wake marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app pairs well with Tap to Wake, respects tap-to-glance workflows, or shows lock-screen content the moment you tap the screen. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Tap to Wake.

An app that references Tap to Wake in onboarding and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe tap-to-wake and tap-to-glance workflows on the store page, not whether Tap to Wake toggles inside iOS Settings.

Tap to Wake-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Tap-to-wake marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Tap to Wake in iOS Settings — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Tap to Wake vs Raise to Wake — do not conflate

US pages sometimes mention both gestures on the same gallery. China storefront copy must keep them distinct: 轻点唤醒 / 点按唤醒 / 轻点屏幕唤醒 / 轻触唤醒 / 点击屏幕唤醒 for tapping the screen when it is face-up and off under Display & Brightness; 抬起唤醒 / 拿起唤醒 for picking up or lifting the phone upright. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope — if your English source only markets Tap to Wake, we do not upgrade to Raise to Wake claims in subtitle, keywords, or overlays.

Official Settings vocabulary

Apple's zh-Hans Settings UI uses 轻点唤醒 for Tap to Wake under 显示与亮度, with related buyer language around 点按唤醒 (tap to wake), 轻点屏幕唤醒 (tap screen to wake), 轻触唤醒 (light touch to wake), and 点击屏幕唤醒 (click/tap screen to wake). Listing copy should mirror that vocabulary — not generic 唤醒屏幕 that could mean Raise to Wake, Face ID unlock, or unrelated power features.

Tap to Wake vs Auto Lock

Auto Lock controls screen timeout before the device locks again — 自动锁定. Tap to Wake controls whether tapping the screen wakes the display from off when face-up. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 自动锁定 when your English source only showed a Tap to Wake toggle. Timeout and tap-to-wake are adjacent settings with different buyer intent.

Tap to Wake vs Always-On Display

Always-On Display keeps a dimmed lock screen visible while the phone rests still — 全天候显示. Tap to Wake wakes the screen when you tap it while off and face-up. zh-Hans copy should not conflate them unless your English page explicitly markets both. See the Always-On Display listing guide only if always-on dimming is your lead marketing claim.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need tap-gesture search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 轻点唤醒, 点按唤醒, and 轻点屏幕唤醒 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Tap to Wake" headlines on gallery frames showing Settings → Display & Brightness → Tap to Wake — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

AppLocale FAQ

Is Tap to Wake the same as Raise to Wake on the listing?

No. Tap to Wake markets tapping the screen when it is face-up and off — 轻点唤醒, 点按唤醒, 轻点屏幕唤醒. Raise to Wake markets lifting or picking up the iPhone — 抬起唤醒, 拿起唤醒. Different gestures, different Connect string families. See our Raise to Wake listing guide for lift-to-wake copy.

Is Tap to Wake the same as Auto Lock?

No. Tap to Wake controls tap-to-wake from off when face-up. Auto Lock controls how long the screen stays on before locking again — 自动锁定. Adjacent Display & Brightness settings, separate listing copy.

Is Tap to Wake the same as Always-On Display?

No. Tap to Wake wakes the screen when you tap it while off and face-up. Always-On Display keeps a dimmed lock screen visible while the phone rests — 全天候显示. See our Always-On Display listing guide for always-on dimming copy.
